tether_sted.citation: Roy, Steinkuehler, Zhao, Lipowsky, Dimova (2020) Nano Lett. 20:3185, doi:10.1021/acs.nanolett.9b05232

tether_sted_verdict: ACCEPTABLE — forces recovered near-unbiased (mean |bias| 3.8%) across the paper's 15-140 uN/m tension range; 68% CIs conservative (coverage 0.90-0.97). This is a real force-paired test: STED-measured tube radius in, measured holding force out.

provenance.citation: Molecular Dynamics Data Bank (MDDB), mddbr.eu; 'A new paradigm for molecular dynamics databases', Nucleic Acids Res. 2024, 52:D393-D403, doi:10.1093/nar/gkad991

mddb_crosscheck.note: MDDB serves structural observables, not stress profiles; this is a parameter cross-check, not a force measurement. Thickness offsets reflect lipid composition / protein content differences between the MD system and the reference POPC value.

mddb_finding: MDDB serves STRUCTURAL membrane observables (thickness, area-per-lipid, lipid-order, density) — NOT stress profiles or tension. It is therefore an independent MD source for curvo's elastic PARAMETERS, not a direct force ground truth. The A020P thickness (3.83 nm, protein-containing bilayer at 303 K) sits 0.44 nm below the pure-POPC reference (4.26 nm): the large z correctly flags a composition mismatch, exactly the diagnostic the cross-check exists to provide.
scope_note: The genuine force-paired validation is the tether/STED test (helfrich_tube geometry). The MDDB adapter adds provenance breadth (a second, orthogonal MD source for structural inputs). Neither replaces the synthetic recovery gate (recovery.py) for the CCS spherical-cap analyze() pipeline.
